app.version: 0.2.41 with the team; going to Apple for outside testers
app.summary:
Smidgeon Scholars, 12 November 2026. Test build 0.2.26 is with testers. This replaces the older "Where the app is now" (0.1.21). Jennie decides what children learn and every word they and their grown-ups hear; Seth's side builds it. Anything marked a draft is Seth's placeholder wording waiting for Jennie.

Five tabs: Today, Journal, Flock, Help me (call Jennie), Settings.

TODAY: one feeling a day, the same for every family (e.g. "The Nervous Feeling"). A journey map of about ten stops in a fixed order: mailbox (the feeling arrives as a group chat with Smidgeon and Jennie), pinwheel (breathing), drum (move your body), Feeling Mirror (make the face, then "What does nervous look like to you? Practice with your grown-up."), Feeling Pairs, a call with Jennie (the child says how they feel; kept on the phone only), the nest, Sun/Cloud/Rainbow, and a present. Each stop ends with a celebration line. The day ends at home: Smidgeon on the windowsill at lunch, dinner, tidy-up or bedtime, with a question and a helper job. The path is once a day.

JOURNAL: a calendar of days, each a postcard: Smidgeon acting out the feeling, the date as a stamp, coins for what we did, and what we said as chat bubbles. How I felt (pick a face) and What we did (coins in Me, Nest, The Flock). A deed done 1/3/5/10 times becomes copper/bronze/silver/gold. Filling in the day is a Stories-style sequence. "Days together" never resets: no broken streaks.

FLOCK (anonymous): a feed of families' postcards with each family's emoji and a made-up kind name, never real names, and hearts. Example families fill it until real ones join. Sharing is off until a grown-up turns it on. Nothing is sent anywhere yet: the real feed (Apple's CloudKit) waits for a children's-privacy (COPPA) review and Jennie's approval of the copy.

HELP ME: call Jennie any time about one feeling.

SETTINGS: tips and printouts, emoji and skin tone, save what we tell Jennie, read everything aloud, flock sharing, narrator voice.

PRINCIPLES: tandem (child and grown-up together); Smidgeon shows, Jennie coaches; steam shows how big a feeling is, never good or bad; never marked wrong; built for pre-readers; resolve and pause before moving on; no red except hang-up and hearts.

HOW TO HELP: suggest wording, order and what children learn in these terms, so Seth's side can drop it straight in. Most words and stories change without a new app version.

tasks.title: Your three learning games: the choices we made
tasks.detail: Built from your docs and in the new test build; the pictures are temporary while we test how they play. Tell us what to change. REMEMBER THREE: same order; Smidgeon asks the child to say them to their grown-up, then they tap them in order from five pictures (three plus two extras: too many?); grows to four after three easy rounds in a row, back to three after a hard one; it lives inside What Did Smidgeon Carry? as see it / hear it. SMIDGEON COUNTS: counts to 10 for now (a 20 setting for four-year-olds, with 12 to 15 in focus, can come next); skills open in your order, each after three first-try successes; both your versions are built (a mix, or one skill a day): which one? Rooftop Hop: child and grown-up take turns rolling for one Smidgeon, dots 1 to 3 at first, bench rest stops are breathing breaks, star roofs bring a skill; Message Route ends with a mailbox or house-number moment. Your try-later lines are used as written; the house-number and adding ones are drafts. Printables later. SMIDGEON'S LETTERS: one of Smidgeon's days a week, up to two new letters a play, then one word; capitals beside lowercase when meeting a letter, lowercase for reading; tracing comes later. The meet lines ("Look! The sun is up.") are drafts: do any scenes or words not fit Smidgeon's world? Digraphs and long vowels later.

tasks.title: The journal's questions
tasks.detail: Filling in the day asks: "What was your sun today?", "What was your cloud today?", "What's your rainbow? Something to look forward to.", "What was your big feeling today?", "What did we do today?". Also the empty-day line "Nothing written down this day." and the button "Fill in today's page".
tasks.answer: Instead of nothing written down this day write, ‘ready for your words’

tasks.title: What we did: the 18 things and their coins
tasks.detail: Me: brushed my teeth, got dressed, packed my lunchbox, ate my veggies, read a book, took a big breath. Nest: put away laundry (Golden Sock), helped with dinner (Golden Fork), put toys away, made my bed, fed a pet, watered plants. The Flock: said thank you (Gratitude Heart), helped a friend, shared, did my schoolwork, cleaned up at school, said hi to someone new. Right 18 for ages 3-5, and the right names? Coins go copper, bronze, silver, gold at 1, 3, 5, 10 times.
tasks.answer: Have a category for the parents to come up with their own chose/task / I think this is a good start, we can always add more later.

tasks.title: "Days together", not streaks
tasks.detail: Count days together and never show a broken streak, with a gold feather icon. Agree, or a Duolingo-style day streak?
tasks.answer: I think keeping days together is age appropriate / Days together not a Duolingo streak

tasks.title: Flock words
tasks.detail: Drafts: "The Flock", "Feeling it together", "Today in the flock", the example-families line, and "Mail from the flock" / "[name] sent a heart". Each family gets a made-up name from a kind word and their child's emoji. Are the kind words right (Little, Brave, Gentle, Busy, Sunny, Sleepy, Hopping, Cosy, Curious, Merry, Quiet, Bouncy)?

tasks.title: Sharing with other families
tasks.detail: Before the real feed goes live: should a child's own words be shareable at all (filtered, names removed on the phone), or only their feeling, coins and emoji? The Settings line "Written down on this phone, never sent anywhere" would need new words. Also needs a children's-privacy (COPPA) review.

tasks.title: Example families' words
tasks.detail: The example families say things like "My blocks fell. I took a big breath." and "We had to leave the park." (two per feeling). Do they sound like real 3-5 year olds? Should the feed say they're examples more or less plainly?

tasks.title: Celebration posts in the flock
tasks.detail: Milestones only at 7, 14, 30, 50, 100 days together ("N days together!", "A day together, again and again."); coins bronze and up ("Earned the Golden Sock!", "Put away laundry, 10 times."). Right moments to celebrate publicly, and right words?
tasks.answer:
They should be sent weekly- it is too long to go beyond seven days for a nod for this age group / It should be 7 days recognition. Not in a row. Just focusing on days together
With a coin on the calendar.

tasks.title: Flock names
tasks.detail: A kind word plus the child's emoji's short name, same first letter: Daring Dino, Bouncy Bunny, Peppy Pup, Kind Kiddo, Lovely Llama, Outdoorsy Otter. Your own reads "Kind Kiddo • Me". Word lists per letter and short names (Pup, Kitty, Dino, Roo, Croc, Spacey) are drafts.
tasks.answer: I think it could be a mix of alliteration and child appropriate adjectives that they can choose from.

tasks.title: The button after the practise-the-face prompt
tasks.detail: After "What does nervous look like to you? Practice with your grown-up.", the family taps "We made the face!" (draft). Keep it, or give the words. Used for all nine feelings.

tasks.title: All the journey's spoken lines
tasks.detail: Every line Smidgeon, Jennie and the narrator say on the journey (hello, breathing, move your body, the call, Sun/Cloud/Rainbow, the present, each stop's celebration). All drafts. Ask Seth's side for the script as a list and mark changes.

tasks.title: End of the day at home
tasks.detail: Titles ("Back to still. Time to tidy up!", "Bedtime soon!", "Time for dinner!"), the question to ask at the table or while tidying, the helper jobs, and the button "Fill in today's journal".

tasks.title: Feeling Pairs and What Did Smidgeon Carry? lines
tasks.detail: Instructions and replies in these two games are drafts (e.g. "Turn over two cards. Can you find two that feel the same?").

tasks.title: Five questions still open from the sync doc
tasks.detail: 1) Emergency or Disaster for the third steam size? 2) Sequencing: unlock skills in order (letters s-a-t-p-i-n) or rotate? 3) Rooftop Hop and Letters: pacing, word lists, the grown-up's role. 4) Older kids: together-only for good, or a Solo mode later? 5) Retype your Message Route comment ("Solo routes add counting..."). The other five (day length, learning areas, Feeling Day, voice, drafted copy) look settled by the journey design or are tasks of their own; Seth to confirm.

tasks.title: Letter sounds
tasks.detail: Smidgeon's Letters is built from your phonics plan and plays placeholder sounds until yours arrive; each recording replaces its placeholder on its own. Pure sounds only (/s/, not "suh"); hold the stretchy ones, keep the bouncy ones crisp; c as /k/, g as /g/, qu as /kw/, x as /ks/. The 26 sounds, by Smidgeon's day: Morning at home: s /sss/ (sun), a /a/ (apple), t /t/ (toast), p /p/ (pan); The mail route: i /i/ (inchworm), n /nnn/ (nest), m /mmm/ (mailbox), d /d/ (door); The garden and pond: g /g/ (gate), o /o/ (otter), c /k/ (cat), k /k/ (kite); A rainy day: r /rrr/ (rain), e /e/ (envelope), u /u/ (umbrella), h /h/ (hat); The park: b /b/ (bus), f /fff/ (feather), l /lll/ (leaf); Lunch and deliveries: j /j/ (jam), w /w/ (worm), v /vvv/ (van), x /ks/ (box); Bedtime: y /y/ (yawn), z /zzz/ (zip), qu /kw/ (quilt). Then each blending word, slowly then quickly ("/s/ /a/ /t/... sat!"): Morning at home: sat, pat, tap, at; The mail route: pin, tin, sit, nap, man, mad, dip, mat; The garden and pond: dog, cat, cap, cot, kid, kit, pot, top, mop; A rainy day: red, hen, ten, net, sun, mud, rug, cup, hug, hot; The park: bed, bus, bug, fan, fig, fun, leg, lip, log; Lunch and deliveries: jam, jog, van, vet, wet, web, wig, box, fox, six; Bedtime: yes, yum, zip, zap, quiz, quit. File names (letter_s, blend_sat…) are in docs/LETTER-SOUNDS.md. Same session as the voice sample is fine.

tasks.title: 18 new Story Path stories (two for every feeling)
tasks.detail: Families who play every day kept meeting the same story: each feeling had one, and a feeling comes round every 9 days. These are 18 drafts, two per feeling, each with a different friend, place and way through. They're already in the app as drafts so Seth can try them. Read each one and reply on it: approve, or say what to change. Approved so far: 11 of 18; 7 still to read.
tasks.answer: Not related but a thought for the welcome message in the app. Who he is. Smidgeon is a carrier pigeon. He carries messages between a child's inner emotional world and the adults who love them. He is "a journal for children who can't write yet."

tasks.title: New draft words from 13 November
tasks.detail: Sun, Cloud and Rainbow now opens with you saying: "Now let's share our sun, our cloud and our rainbow. Your sun is something that brought you joy today. Your cloud is something that was hard. Your rainbow is something you're looking forward to." (Seth wonders if it's too long for 3–5s.) Today's journal page title is "A … day" until a feeling is picked, then "A sad day"; its prompts are "I told Jennie…", "My sun today was…", "My cloud today was…", "My rainbow is…", "What I did today…"; a past day with nothing written says "Nothing written down this day."; the feeling picker asks "How are you feeling today?". The finished day's button: "Fill in today's journal" / "See today's journal".

tasks.title: Pick Smidgeon's new voice
tasks.detail: Listen to today's voice and eight candidates (A to H), each saying the same calm, sad and bright lines. Reply here with the letter you like, or two letters to mix, and all of Smidgeon's lines will be re-recorded in that voice.
